parts.visual:
A CEO looks at the company data. They have 1,000 customers, but they realize that 80% of their total profit comes from just 200 of those customers.

The Principle:
1. The Rule: 80% of the effects come from 20% of the causes.
2. The Application: 20% of your sales team generates 80% of your revenue. 20% of your products cause 80% of your customer complaints.
3. The Executive Action: Firing the bottom 80% of bad customers, and obsessing over the top 20%.
parts.audio: The Pareto Principle, or the 80/20 rule, states that eighty percent of outcomes come from twenty percent of causes. Elite executives use this mathematical rule to violently prioritize their time and resources.

questions.question: A software company has 50 features. The data shows that users only ever click on 10 of those features. The engineers want to spend millions updating the 40 unused features. What should the CEO do?
options: Apply the Pareto Principle. Delete the 40 unused features entirely to save money, and invest all the engineering budget into making the core 10 features absolutely perfect.
questions.correct_answer: Apply the Pareto Principle. Delete the 40 unused features entirely to save money, and invest all the engineering budget into making the core 10 features absolutely perfect.
questions.explanation: Complexity is the enemy of execution. The 80/20 rule helps you cut the fat.

questions.question: Listen to the Sales Director. What shocking strategy is he proposing?
questions.tts_text: I analyzed our client list. 80 percent of our tech support tickets and legal headaches come from our lowest-paying clients. I am officially firing our worst 50 clients tomorrow.
options: Firing the bottom tier. By eliminating the 80% of clients who cause all the problems but generate very little revenue, he frees up the company to focus on the VIPs.
questions.correct_answer: Firing the bottom tier. By eliminating the 80% of clients who cause all the problems but generate very little revenue, he frees up the company to focus on the VIPs.
questions.explanation: Not all revenue is good revenue. Some customers literally cost more to maintain than they pay you.

questions.question: How does the Pareto Principle apply to an executive's personal time management?
options: They should work 80 hours a week.
20% of the tasks on a CEO's desk will generate 80% of the value for the company. The CEO must delegate or ignore the other 80% of 'busywork'.
They should sleep 20 hours a day.
questions.correct_answer: 20% of the tasks on a CEO's desk will generate 80% of the value for the company. The CEO must delegate or ignore the other 80% of 'busywork'.
questions.explanation: Average managers try to do everything. Elite executives only do the few things that actually matter.

questions.question: What is the danger of ignoring the Pareto Principle when designing a marketing budget?
options: You will spread your budget equally across 10 different marketing channels, even though the data shows that only 2 of those channels are actually generating all the sales. It is a massive waste of capital.
questions.correct_answer: You will spread your budget equally across 10 different marketing channels, even though the data shows that only 2 of those channels are actually generating all the sales. It is a massive waste of capital.
questions.explanation: Equality is a terrible strategy in capital allocation. You must double-down on the winners.
